note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a LEB 3; A06b LEB 3; L05 No provision): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen keeps it on taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Gender restriction: no or restricted access if the mother is a citizen (wedlock condition/supplementary provision may apply)), A01b (descent, born abroad: Gender restriction: no or restricted access if the mother is a citizen (wedlock condition/supplementary provision may apply)), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from the father only, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Lebanon, 2024
sources.said: Person has lived in country for 5 consecutive years. May be granted by Head of State. ... n.a. ... n.a. ... Gender restriction: no or restricted access if the mother is a citizen (wedlock condition/supplementary provision may apply) ... Person is born in Lebanon to a male citizen. (In Lebanon, there is a problem with individuals who are born [to a Lebanese mother] out of wedlock not being able to have their birth registered. Lack of birth registration may result in problems with not being considered a citizen. This can be resolved in court, but this is not a simple process. We are not aware of any legal provisions that allow access to citizenship by mother if illegitimate, and on the ground we have never seen cases where this takes place.) ... Gender restriction: no or restricted access if the mother is a citizen (wedlock condition/supplementary provision may apply) ... Person is born abroad to a male citizen. (In Lebanon, there is a problem with individuals who are born out of wedlock not being able to have their birth registered. Lack of birth registration may result in problems with not being considered a citizen. This can be resolved in court, but this is not a simple process. We are not aware of any legal provisions that allow access to citizenship by mother if illegitimate, and on the ground we have never seen cases where this takes place.) ... No provision ...
